user_prompt: Draft a reply to my landlord contesting a $75 late fee. Reference Section 4.2 of the lease and the grace period it establishes, and state clearly that my payment was on time. Firm, polite, no apologies, 120 words max.
final_prompt:
Draft a reply to my landlord contesting a $75 late fee. Reference Section 4.2 of the lease and the grace period it establishes, and state clearly that my payment was on time. Firm, polite, no apologies, 120 words max.

<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Subject: Re: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

I'm writing to dispute the $75 late fee on my account for this month's rent.

Section 4.2 of our lease states that rent is due on the 1st and that a grace period applies through the 5th, during which no late fees may be charged. My payment was received on the 3rd, which falls within that grace period. The fee is therefore not permitted under the lease.

Please remove the $75 charge from my account and confirm in writing. I'll pay next month's rent as usual, without the fee.

Thank you,
